datasets: NIBRS Group A Crime Data (Open Baltimore ArcGIS FeatureServer, 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-31, data/live/crime.json)
BPD Arrests (Open Baltimore / baltegis GeoSpatialized_Tables/Arrest FeatureServer, same window, data/live/arrests.json)
concurrency_primitives: 2 goroutines fetch both ArcGIS sources with context cancellation (ingest.go:150-170); 2 goroutines decode both JSON files (main.go:60-70); crime aggregation worker pool: bounded jobs channel (2*workers), N workers with private partial Result maps, partials channel, feeder goroutine + WaitGroup, sequential reducer (analysis.go:36-83); arrest pre-pass, cross-tabs and incident index are sequential
design_patterns: Pipeline (ingest -> normalize -> analyze -> report, one file per stage) with map-reduce style worker pool; no Builder/Strategy/Factory
questions: Which neighborhoods have the largest recorded crime workload, and how does arrest activity compare?
How do monthly crime and arrest workloads change?
What offense mix is recorded in the five neighborhoods with the most arrest records?
Where are crime-record and arrest-record shares most different by neighborhood?
What weapon profile and arrest workload occur in the five neighborhoods with the most crime records?
overview: Compact single-package Go organized by pipeline stage (ingest, normalize, analysis, report) with its own paginated ArcGIS fetcher, provenance manifest, schema checks and httptest-backed tests. Rows are loosely typed map[string]any decoded fully into memory; the report is one dense function and variable names are terse, but the README is careful, accurate and heavily caveated.
stakeholder_value: All five questions are aggregate crime-by-arrest joins by neighborhood or month, honestly qualified by the fact that 69% of arrest rows lack a neighborhood. Q4 (Downtown holds 3.6% of crime but 8.3% of geocoded arrests) is the one finding a leader would act on; Q2 is a plain monthly count and Q3/Q5 mix differences are small. Purposes are stated but no municipal office is named, and visualization is one ASCII chart plus tables.
issues: Stakeholders are generic purposes ('for staffing review') rather than named municipal offices
Concurrency covers I/O and one aggregation stage only; arrest aggregation, cross-tabs and incident index are sequential passes
Rows are map[string]any and both JSON files are decoded fully into memory (98 MB RSS for 12 MB input)
Only one ASCII chart; remaining output is Markdown tables
69% of arrest rows have no neighborhood so most answers describe a 31% subset (disclosed)
README is Windows-first (macOS section present and correct); run.sh writes binary and report into the project folder
rationale: Full credit for build, data, run and README: the program fetched real NIBRS crime and BPD arrest records through its own ArcGIS client, bundles them with a manifest, defaults to the real snapshot, and reproduces the shipped report exactly with clean vet, tests and race detector. Deductions for partial concurrency (one parallel stage), a loosely typed in-memory data model, a single-package layout without realized design patterns, and cross-dataset questions that are sound but shallow and addressed to unnamed stakeholders with minimal visualization. Total 82, B.
